column3: The Hebrew describes lying down with his fathers and active plural buriers; BSB says rested and expresses burial passively.
The Hebrew has singular commandment; BSB uses plural commandments.
The Hebrew says the kingdom rested before him; BSB says under him.
The Hebrew leaves the builder unnamed and calls the period years; BSB names Asa and says days.
The Hebrew says the land is still before us; BSB says still ours.
The Hebrew says a thousand thousands and has singular he came; BSB uses 1,000,000 and plural they advanced.
The Hebrew has a plural subject for drawing up for battle; BSB continues with Asa as the singular subject.
The Hebrew speaks of helping between the great and one without strength; BSB explicitly says helping the powerless against the mighty.

The Hebrew names the people with Asa and leaves the plunderers implicit; BSB calls the pursuers his army and explicitly names the people of Judah as plunderers. The force with the LORD is called His camp rather than His army.
The Hebrew says tents of livestock and uses a capturing verb; BSB says tents of the herdsmen and carried off.
